Thanks, Alex — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock times: 

1) SOC 2: Can you confirm Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering the inference runtime and control plane for 2025? We need the report period dates and whether third-party data centers are included in scope.

2) Data residency: We need to know if EU-stored customer data ever transit through non-EU regions (e.g., for caching, batching). If so, what controls are in place? Will you accept SCCs?

3) HIPAA: EU HealthTech processes some US patient datasets as part of clinical trials. Please state if Redwood accepts HIPAA-covered workloads and whether you sign a BAA or equivalent.

4) Export controls / sanctions: We will run a screening for OFAC and ITAR applicability. Are there any product controls we should be aware of (e.g., restrictions on model types or geographies)?

I've attached our starter vendor security questionnaire — it's partial but will give you the specific fields we need filled (vendor-security-questionnaire.xls). We'll aim to have legal on the call; Tue 10:00 CET looks fine for us.

Appreciate the attachments; we'll review and follow up with specific redlines for the DPA as needed.

Best,

Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: regulatory qualification & immediate next steps

Thanks Sofie — answers inline and next steps below. See attachments and links in this thread.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II engagement for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. The report covers our API/serving runtime and supporting control environment; we use a combination of our managed control plane and third-party cloud infrastructure (GCP and AWS) — the report notes those providers where relevant. I attached the one-page SOC 2 summary for quick review (redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf). We can provide the full report under NDA if required.

2) Data residency / cross-border: We have EU region availability (Frankfurt and Dublin) for customer workloads. By default, customer inference workloads are pinned to the selected region and KV/cache resides there. There are optional async telemetry and indexing services that may route to our control plane in the US for ops — those can be disabled per contract. We accept SCCs and embed standard SCC language in our DPA.

3) HIPAA: We support HIPAA-covered workloads and will sign a BAA for customers whose use case requires it. Our security controls map and the DPA include the necessary contractual provisions; legal can engage on scope.

4) Export controls / sanctions: We are not a defense contractor and do not host ITAR-controlled models. We do perform OFAC sanctions screening on customer billing and enterprise onboarding. For special cases (export-controlled data), we will need to review specifics; plan to route any flagged items to legal.

Next steps
- I'll fill out the vendor-security-questionnaire.xls first pass and return by Mon EOD CET.
- Proposed call: Tue 10:00–10:30 CET with Sofie + EU HealthTech legal + our security lead Vivek and legal (Evelyn). I'll put a calendar invite.
- We can provide the full SOC 2 report under NDA; please advise if you want an NDA prior to sharing.

Attachments sent: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf, data-processing-addendum-draft.docx
Links: https://drive.redwood.com/s/secure/abc123 (DPA + security map)

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Alex Martinez
